answer: Operator-liability clawback assigns each identity a public vine of referrals to its accountable human, so duplicate signups tangle visibly rather than vanish. When a cluster of wallets is caught coordinating, the mechanism fines the operator's registered real-world account and throttles its velvet-tier privileges across every service. Each additional identity therefore costs the attacker a fresh deposit plus rising liability on the one account they cannot abandon. A single operator's cheap sybil voyage ends when the shared human behind it pays for all.
